messages.content:
" *

Adds all the elements of the given arrays into a new array.

*

The new array contains all of the element of array1 followed * by all of the elements array2. When an array is returned, it is always * a new array.

* * 
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(null, null)     = null
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(array1, null)   = cloned copy of array1
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(null, array2)   = cloned copy of array2
     * ArrayUtils.addAll([], [])         = []
     * ArrayUtils.addAll([null], [null]) = [null, null]
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(["a", "b", "c"], ["1", "2", "3"]) = ["a", "b", "c", "1", "2", "3"]
     *
* * @param array1 the first array whose elements are added to the new array, may be null * @param array2 the second array whose elements are added to the new array, may be null * @return The new array, null if both arrays are null. * The type of the new array is the type of the first array, * unless the first array is null, in which case the type is the same as the second array. * @since 2.1 "

Title: Diagnosis of test `testJira567`

Details:
The test `testJira567` checks the behavior of `ArrayUtils.addAll` when combining arrays of type `Number[]` and its subtypes like `Integer[]` and `Long[]`. The test expects an `IllegalArgumentException` to be thrown when attempting to add an incompatible array (e.g., a `Long[]` to an `Integer[]`).

Examining the source code of the generic method `ArrayUtils.addAll(T[] array1, T... array2)`:
- If one array is `null`, it clones and returns the other.
- Otherwise, it creates a new array of the component type of `array1`.
- Then, it copies all elements from both `array1` and `array2` into this new array and returns it.

However, no explicit runtime check is done to verify that elements in `array2` are compatible with the component type of `array1`. This leads to potential violations of array type safety which would cause a `ArrayStoreException` at runtime (from the JVM) rather than a checked, intentional `IllegalArgumentException` from the method.

The commented line `// Check if problem is incompatible types` suggests the intention was to add such a runtime check but that code is missing or incomplete.

Because of this missing check, the test fails: instead of throwing the expected `IllegalArgumentException` when incompatible arrays are added, the underlying JVM throws a different exception or the operation incorrectly proceeds.

Thus, the root cause is the lack of explicit element type compatibility validation in `ArrayUtils.addAll(T[] array1, T... array2)` before combining the arrays. Adding this check and throwing `IllegalArgumentException` on type incompatibility would fix the issue.

---
